results.evidence: The commitment column's VI is clearly out of line with a two-day spring snow/ice route (grade III-IV in the row), but no external source found states a commitment numeral for the X Couloir: the published trip reports rate it only by its ice crux (AI3+) and Wikipedia gives only time (~9 hours) and hazards. results.fact: Approach side (Rankin Creek from FR-38 vs Heliotrope Ridge and the Coleman/Deming glaciers)
results.correct_value: This row's plan is the FR-38 / Rankin Creek approach to a ~6,100 ft treeline camp; the partner requirements, crevasse note and permit note should describe that approach, not a Heliotrope/Coleman-Deming glacier approach.
results.evidence: Three independent trip reports describe the X Couloir approach by NF-38 (Middle Fork Nooksack) to the switchbacks, then up the Rankin Creek basin to camp at ~6,000-6,100 ft at the highest trees above Wallace Creek, with the crux at the bergschrund/serac of the southwest basin. None crosses the Coleman or Deming glaciers. (Heliotrope is a genuine alternative via the Thunder Glacier cirque — logged separately — but it is not the approach this row's itinerary, approach and variant describe.)

results.fact: Whether Heliotrope Ridge can reach the X Couloir
results.evidence: The approach, variant notes, baseFinding and descent_text insist Heliotrope serves only the NW face and must not be used. Wikipedia says the southwest face is reached from the Heliotrope Ridge Trail via the Thunder Glacier cirque, with the Middle Fork road as an alternative, and one trip report chose Rankin Creek because it looked slightly shorter than the Heliotrope approach — implying Heliotrope is a real alternative. The row's exclusivity claim looks wrong, but rewriting four prose fields needs a firmer second source on the Heliotrope/Thunder line.

results.correct_value: This row is the Wilkes-Booth line on the NW face, first climbed by Daniel Coltrane and Michal Rynkiewicz on March 13, 2015; the 1958 Cooper/O'Conner climb is a different line (the north flank) and should not be presented as this route.

results.evidence: The first-ascent party descended the southwest face and still finished at the Heliotrope Ridge trailhead in an 18.5-hour round trip, and the southwest face's cirque (Thunder Glacier) is reached from the Heliotrope Ridge Trail, so descending the SW face and returning to the Coleman and Heliotrope is a documented link, not a landing in the Rankin Creek basin.

No outside source states a car-to-car gain or loss for the Wilkes-Booth round trip (the AAC report gives only length, grade and 18.5 hours). Under the rules gain_ft/loss_ft change only to a sourced figure, so the 5,500 vs 6,400 ft discrepancy stays open.
